items.title: Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2010
items.q: or you want to use the techniques used by Ornette Coleman

ctx.x: Well you’re right, you have to have some understanding of harmonically what’s going on. But I will say you try to learn all of these various techniques and your phrases that you’re learning and themes, and then hopefully you can go on stage with the clean slate. And then you can just create based on what is provided to you by your musical environment at that particular time. So the pianist is feeding you something, the bass player is feeding you something, and the drummer is feeding you something, and I’m,…

learn from somebody how we do what we do. Nobody just took a baby and just left them there, they wouldn’t make it. You’ve got to have some kind of development, so you’ve got to at some point recognize the techniques and use some part of the technique whether you want to come from the technique of Charlie Parker or you want to use the technique of Lester Young or you want to use the techniques used by Ornette Coleman or John Coltrane or Sun Ra or somebody. But you’ve got to pull from somewhere.
Probably someone has asked you in the past about your grounding, of those artists. Who do you feel you sort of came out of?
